answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using trust-graph routing. Nodes maintain signed interaction channels, while a consensus beacon samples random walks to detect graph bottlenecks. This forces adversaries to expend scarce relational capital securing authentic edges with honest peers instead of spawning clones behind a sable veil of virtual addresses. However, high bootstrapping friction strands legitimate newcomers in an unverified trust lagoon until established nodes vouch for them.
